reason: The transporter-bearing cell can take in the arriving glucose, starting the path toward usable energy.
expectation: Glucose and oxygen will become available to the cell for energy production.

effect: The cell instead combined with the fibre structures, establishing the muscle fibre scaffold. I still need to find how the fuel enters the energy pathway.
reaction: I was surprised that the cell could not combine directly with the arriving fuel.
reason: Mitochondria are associated with releasing usable energy from fuel, so the fuel and oxygen are a plausible next pairing.
expectation: The mitochondria will use the glucose and oxygen in an energy-producing process.

effect: The fuel and oxygen produced fuelled mitochondria; the picture also shows glucose being split in the cell fluid before smaller molecules enter the mitochondrion.
reaction: The distinction between the cell fluid and mitochondrion clarified the process for me.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the available pieces for making ATP, and the fuelled mitochondria appear ready to supply the energy.
expectation: The fuelled mitochondria will help turn ADP and phosphate into ATP.

effect: The fuelled mitochondria produced an ATP supply, and the picture shows ADP and phosphate returning as ATP is used.
reaction: The cycle makes the need for a continuing energy supply clearer.
reason: The thin actin and thick myosin filaments look like complementary parts of the fibre’s pulling machinery.
expectation: The filaments will form a contractile unit that can later be fitted into the muscle fibre.

effect: The actin and myosin filaments formed sliding filament units, which appear ready to fit into the muscle fibre.
reaction: Their overlapping arrangement makes the pulling mechanism easier to picture.
reason: The fibre scaffold has spaces for contractile units, so the sliding filament units should fit there.
expectation: The filament units will be installed in the muscle fibre.

effect: The sliding filament units are now installed in the muscle fibre. The fibre still needs the conditions for pulling and relaxing.
reason: The calcium signal reaches the filaments and is a plausible trigger for a pull.
expectation: The calcium signal will activate the fibre’s pulling machinery.

effect: The fibre needed an ATP supply before the calcium signal could act. It is now ATP-ready, with myosin heads able to release and reset.
reaction: The required order surprised me, but the close-up helps explain ATP’s role.
reason: The calcium signal is still available and may now expose the covered binding sites so the fibre can pull.
expectation: Calcium will activate the filament machinery and allow the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium activated the ATP-ready fibre, and the picture shows that the fibre shortens as filaments slide rather than shorten themselves.
reaction: The distinction between the shortening fibre and unchanged filament lengths is clear.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes appear suited to return calcium to storage, allowing the fibre to relax.
expectation: The membranes will pump calcium back into storage so the fibre can relax and prepare for another pull.

effect: The calcium-pumping membranes completed the relaxation cycle: ATP powers calcium’s return to storage, grip sites become covered, and pulling stops.
reaction: I found it satisfying that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Activating the fibre with calcium was most worthwhile: the result connects the signal to myosin’s pull and distinguishes shortening of the fibre from sliding of the filaments.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the filament-filled fibre was straightforward, but the two assembly steps contributed less explanation than the later close-ups.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the fibre needed ATP before the calcium signal could act. The result showed ATP helping myosin release and reset.

arbitrary.text: The first attempt to combine the cell with arriving fuel felt unintuitive: the game instead directed the cell into a fibre scaffold. The feedback made the next action clear, though.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in seeing how the muscle fibre connects to larger tissues and body systems, because this chapter made the relationship between ATP, calcium and movement concrete.
